accuracy.evidence: Definitions match PSHE Association and NHS/Childline usage: assertive = saying what you need calmly while respecting others (not 'always winning', m7); passive = hiding your need (p2, m1); aggressive = attacking, blaming or threatening (m2); I-statement = 'I feel ... when ... could we ...' naming a feeling plus the action (p3, m4); negotiate = the two sides talk it out, mediate = a neutral helper in the middle (p5, m8), resolution = the agreed fix (m5), boundary = a line for how others treat you (m6). Compromise = both give a little (p4, step 3 needs tag 8-12 of 20 minutes).

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the known confusions: being quiet and nice equals assertive (m1, challenge tag 'nice'), assertive means getting your way (m7), 'I feel like you are mean' counts as an I-statement though it is a label (step 2 trap tag 'label', m4), 'always/never' blame (tag 'always'), one side giving in counts as compromise (p4 choice 'Ben gives in', step 3 'One wins, one loses'), and mixing up negotiate vs mediate (step 4 special feedback, p5, tag 'mixup').

lab_distinct.evidence: flag_assert.js is built around social-communication interactions found in no other flagship lab: a quiet-to-loud style track where Jo and Kai react to each tone, a three-bin passive/assertive/aggressive sorter with reasoned feedback, an I-statement builder that rejects blame/label/always phrases, and a draggable divider sharing a 20-minute break. It passed the lab_distinct shingle gate against flagcit (bystanders) and flagemo (feelings).

lab_teaches.evidence: Each step practises one idea from the lesson by doing: hearing the same reply in three styles, classifying six replies, assembling an I-statement in the right order (I feel / when / Could we) and choosing non-blaming parts, physically negotiating a fair split of break time, and matching conflict, negotiate, mediate, resolution and boundary to concrete scenes. Done lines name what was learned.

predictions.evidence: Learners commit before acting: step 0 asks whether shouting will get Kai his pencil back fastest and best, step 2 asks which opening helps the other person listen, step 3 asks what makes a plan a compromise; wrong options get specific explanations (shouting works short-term but damages the friendship).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Five mixed challenge questions (style spotting, assertive reply in a lunch-line push-in, I-statement repair, compromise, mediate vs negotiate). Every wrong option carries a slip tag (passive, aggro, blame, givein, mixup, nice) whose feedback names the exact slip rather than just 'wrong', and the run ends with a score and a retry.

readability.evidence: Learner audience for ages 7-11: kid paragraphs use short sentences and everyday scenes (pencils, swings, break-time games) and the validator readability gate passed against the 6.5 kid / 9.5 adult targets; conflict words are always introduced with an example scene before the label.

no_filler.evidence: Content gate passed with no filler phrases and low overlap; every paragraph either defines a style, shows the I-statement pattern, explains compromise vs giving in, or gives adults the common mistakes (assertive mistaken for loud, quiet-and-nice mistaken for assertive, 'I feel like you are rude', always/never, negotiate vs mediate) and how the lab practises each.

mobile.evidence: walk.cjs on iPhone 13 completed all 6 steps, 5 tasks and the challenge with no console errors; screenshots on iPhone (light) and a 360x640 Android (dark) show cards, bins and the break bar fit the width, drag targets are large, and every drag has tap-button alternatives (More tag / More football, style buttons, match buttons).

accessibility.evidence: axe returned zero violations in both light and dark themes on desktop and phone; every control has an aria-label, drag interactions have button equivalents, status text is announced through the say line, and colour is never the only cue (bins carry words and emoji, the track has text labels).

NHS Every Mind Matters and Childline guidance on being assertive and using 'I' statements
